MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Director of Research and Innovation





Job no: 943929

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Science, Engineering, Technical




 
Central Adelaide Local Health Network

Statewide - SA Pathology

MeS6B $170,363 p.a. (pro-rata) + Superannuation & Salary Sacrifice Benefits

Located in: Adelaide CBD 

Full Time, Temporary 3 Year Contract Available Role 

About the role

As the Director of Research and Innovation (Governance & Strategy), you will play a pivotal leadership role in shaping the strategic direction, governance, and performance of SA Pathology's research portfolio. Providing expert leadership to the Clinical Service Director and Executive Director, you will establish and operationalise a contemporary, integrated Research & Innovation capability, embed a Research Charter, and implement a Governance Framework with clear accountability, decision-making pathways, and measurable outcomes.

Working collaboratively across disciplines, you will drive implementation of an integrated research operating model that ensures robust governance and connects strategy, delivery, compliance, and assurance. You will lead the optimisation of governance structures, establishing clear roles, responsibilities, and decision rights while strengthening risk, ethics, and compliance systems to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements and best practice standards.

You will champion a culture of innovation and collaboration, fostering strategic partnerships with government, academia, and industry to identify, develop, and commercialise new discoveries. As an influential leader and change agent, you will position SA Pathology as a research partner of choice, strengthening its national and global reputation for excellence in scientific advancement. Through strong governance, strategic foresight, and a focus on innovation and commercial opportunity, you will enable SA Pathology to deliver world-class research that informs policy, practice, and system-wide improvement.

About You

You are a strategic and transformative research leader with a strong background in medical science and a proven ability to drive innovation, governance reform, and organisational change within complex research environments. With experience leading multidisciplinary teams and fostering partnerships across academia, industry and government, you demonstrate both strategic insight and operational expertise. You are an engaging communicator, an effective problem-solver, and a passionate advocate for advancing clinical research that delivers real-world health outcomes.

In this role, you will bring:

- Qualifications & Professional Background

Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Applied Science (Medical Laboratory Science) or equivalent; supported by extensive experience leading government translational and commercial research programs.

- Strategic Leadership & Transformation

Demonstrated experience leading research transformation through governance reform and operating model design, develop project plans and timelines, and engage diverse stakeholders with vision and influence.

 - Governance, Risk & Compliance

Strong expertise in research governance, financial and contract management, regulatory compliance, and ethical frameworks, with a proven ability to define decision-making structures, accountabilities, and assurance processes.

- Collaboration & Influence

Highly developed communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills, with demonstrated ability to build and sustain cross-sector partnerships and experience embedding research into clinical and operational practice.

About us

Statewide Clinical Support Services (SCSS) is a unique public healthcare organisation that serves health consumers and provides specialist clinical services to the health system in South Australia. SCSS encompasses BreastScreen SA, SA Dental, SA Medical Imaging, SA Pathology, and SA Pharmacy. Come and work with us to improve the health and well-being of South Australians, across all age groups and at any time of their life or health need. 

What we offer

Salary Benefits: Enjoy flexible salary packaging options, including up to $9,010 each FBT year for living expenses (such as mortgage, rent, utilities and groceries) plus an additional $2,650 for meal and entertainment expenses.

Professional Development: Opportunity to apply for reimbursement of eligible professional development activities, and access to dedicated leave for ongoing learning.

Annual Leave: Enjoy paid recreation leave for essential rejuvenation, with leave loading applied.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program for you and your family, plus an annual voluntary flu vaccination to support your wellbeing.

Employee Assistance Program: Confidential counselling and support services for you and your family via our Employee Assistance Program.

Diversity and inclusion:

Statewide supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe at work. The culture aims to encourage all people to use their talents and to be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are encouraged to apply. 

Application Information:

Please refer to the role description for essential educational-vocational qualifications that may be required.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and compliant Immunisation screening as indicated in the role description.

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Please note that unsolicited applications from recruitment agencies or third parties will not be accepted for this position.

result.description:
Lead electrical mining projects from concept to commissioning while enjoying a 5:2 roster   Your new company  
 Our client is a leading Australian resources organisation with a strong commitment to operational excellence, safety, and sustainable project delivery. With a substantial portfolio of capital projects and ongoing investment in site infrastructure, they offer the opportunity to work on complex projects within a collaborative and high-performing team environment. 
   Your new role  
 As an Electrical Project Manager, you will be responsible for managing electrical capital projects through the full project life cycle, from early studies and detailed design through to construction, commissioning, and handover. You will work closely with consultants, contractors, and key stakeholders to deliver projects safely, on schedule, and within budget. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Managing electrical projects from concept development through to completion 
 Coordinating consultants during feasibility studies, engineering, and detailed design phases 
 Managing project budgets, schedules, risks, and reporting requirements 
 Overseeing contractors and ensuring compliance with contractual obligations 
 Leading project execution, construction activities, and commissioning works 
 Reviewing and managing project documentation, technical deliverables, and governance requirements 
 Collaborating with operations, maintenance, engineering, and external stakeholders 
 Ensuring all work is delivered in line with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements 
 Driving project performance and continuous improvement outcomes 
 
   What you'll need to succeed     
 
 Demonstrated experience managing electrical projects within mining, resources, heavy industry, energy, or infrastructure environments 
 Proven experience managing consultants through study, design, and project delivery phases 
 Strong understanding of project delivery methodologies and project governance requirements 
 Experience managing contractors during construction and commissioning activities 
 Sound knowledge of contract administration and contractor management 
 Strong stakeholder engagement, communication, and leadership skills 
 Ability to manage multiple project priorities in a dynamic operational environment 
 Electrical trade or engineering qualifications will be highly regarded. 
 Commitment to maintaining the highest safety standards 
 
   What you'll get in return  
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a highly regarded mining operation and contribute to the successful delivery of critical electrical infrastructure projects. You'll work on a Monday-to-Thursday site roster with the flexibility to work from home on Fridays, while camp accommodation is provided throughout your assignment. Both FIFO and DIDO options are available, offering flexibility for candidates across Queensland. You'll join a supportive team environment where your expertise will directly influence the success of key site projects and future growth initiatives. 
   What you need to do now  
 If you're interested in this role, applications can be submitted via the "apply now" button. Please ensure you are submitting an up-to-date CV. If you have any further questions, please call Jennah Murray 07 4960 1129. 
   
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.  Please  click here  to apply.

Position: Construction Project Manager
Position Type: Full Time
Salary: $110,000 - $130,000 p.a plus Super
Employer Name: J & DE HOMES PTY LTD - T/a JDE HOMES
A.B.N. 24 614 743 789
Job Location: Level 2, 207 Pulteney Street, Adelaide, SA, 5000,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 28 days - 13 Jul 2026 > 10 Aug 2026

Please include Reference: J1697-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Our client JDE Homes is seeking to add a Construction Project Manager to its South Australian construction and development team. The company delivers fixed-price property construction, development and project management services across residential, civil, industrial and commercial projects. This role will support the planning, coordination and delivery of technically challenging building projects, while maintaining quality, budget, safety and completion requirements.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Plan, organise and manage construction projects from commencement through to practical completion.
- Coordinate project resources, including labour, subcontractors, materials, plant and equipment.
- Interpret architectural drawings, construction plans, engineering details and technical specifications.
- Monitor project budgets, timelines, quality standards, risks and contractual obligations.
- Liaise with architects, engineers, consultants, clients, subcontractors and relevant authorities.
- Manage procurement scheduling and ensure materials are available to meet construction milestones.
- Supervise site progress and ensure works align with approved plans and specifications.
- Coordinate inspections, approvals and documentation required by councils and regulatory bodies.
- Ensure adherence to workplace health, safety, building and performance standards.
- Negotiate with suppliers, subcontractors and stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.
- Prepare project reports, progress updates, cost reviews and construction documentation.
- Manage project variations, delays, defects and implementation of corrective actions.
- Lead subcontractors and site teams to achieve quality and programme outcomes.
- Support tender preparation, contract administration and construction methodology recommendations.
- Maintain professional communication with clients to support cost-effective project delivery.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- Minimum ten years of relevant experience in construction project management or building project delivery.
- Strong ability to manage residential, commercial, civil or industrial construction projects from start to finish.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating subcontractors, trades, consultants, suppliers, plant, equipment and site resources.
- Sound knowledge of construction drawings, specifications, building processes, safety obligations and quality standards.
- Proven ability to monitor project costs, budgets, schedules, risks, variations and completion deadlines.
- Strong communication skills for liaising with clients, architects, engineers, authorities and internal project teams.
- Practical experience resolving construction issues and recommending cost-effective building methods or project solutions.
- Ability to work without direct supervision while maintaining accurate project records and professional standards.

Please include Reference: J1697-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.

Salary: $74,095 - $78,694 per annum + Super + Benefits 

Full Time, Temporary - to 29th January 2027 

WHAT ARE WE OFFERING? 

We are offering a 6-month temporary opportunity to provide high-level, confidential executive support to the Executive Director People and Culture. This role offers exposure to senior leadership, involvement in key coordination and project support activities, and the chance to contribute to the smooth operation of critical People and Culture functions across the network. It also provides valuable professional development opportunities, allowing you to broaden your skills, gain insight into strategic workforce initiatives, and build experience working within a senior executive environment. This is an excellent opportunity to enhance your career profile, expand your professional networks, and develop capabilities that can support future career progression within SA Health.

WHO ARE WE? 

The Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network offers opportunities across our sites, from Kangaroo Island to Eudunda, wrapping all the way around our metropolitan areas. We pride ourselves on providing exceptional care to all our consumers, residents, their families, and community. Our mission is to ensure that you always receive the best quality, safe, consistent, collaborative care and always with kindness. We do this by maintaining exceptional levels of care at all times supported by systems and processes that assure us of quality and safety of our staff and those we serve. 

 WHERE AND HOW YOU WILL WORK 

This role allows for flexibility to work from any of our BHFLHN sites by negotiation, or the ability to work remotely, and benefit from the work-life balance this provides.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

Do you have experience delivering high-level, confidential executive and administrative support in a fast-paced environment? 

Are you an effective communicator who can build strong relationships with senior stakeholders and diverse internal and external partners? 

Can you manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgement, and maintain strict confidentiality while delivering accurate, high-quality work? 

Are you a collaborative team player with strong organisational and systems skills, committed to continuous improvement, cultural sensitivity, and excellent customer service? 

If you have answered yes to any of these questions - then read on. 

HOW WILL YOU CONTRIBUTE? 

You will.... 

You will deliver high-quality, confidential executive and administrative support, ensuring efficient daily operations and timely communication across the service. 

You will coordinate and support projects by tracking progress, conducting research, and liaising with stakeholders to achieve outcomes. 

You will maintain effective systems and processes, contributing to continuous improvement and ensuring compliance with policies and procedures. 

You will foster strong working relationships and provide culturally appropriate, customer-focused support to both internal and external stakeholders. 

WHAT WILL WE OFFER YOU IN RETURN? 

At BHFLHN, not only will you be working in an environment surrounded by beautiful scenery and nature we see your work here as not just as a job, but an opportunity to extend, progress or consolidate your career with us. We therefore offer you opportunities to be supported in the following ways: 

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT year Click here more information 

Access to generous leave provisions and professional development opportunities. 

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program. 

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program available to BHFLHN staff and their families. 

WHAT ELSE DO YOU NEED TO KNOW-WHAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR SUCCESS? 

Working in this environment, it is important to us that we only employ people with the upmost integrity and commitment to serving the South Australian community and its visitors to the highest possible standards. To ensure that we meet that commitment there are a few checks that you will be required to undertake. These are detailed on the Role Description, but are likely to include the following: 

You will need to be immunised. Please contact the Enquiries Person for this position if you have any queries. Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy. Further information is in the application for to help guide you. 

You will need to undergo employment screening, what you require is also on the front page of the Role Description. 

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION 

We employ people as diverse as the clients we support and the environments we work in. At BHFLHN we pride ourselves on being an Equal Opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees and therefore we encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, disability, all genders, and LGBTQI+ community. 

NEED TO RELOCATE? 

Relocation financial support may be negotiated, subject to eligibility. See what is available here: Relocation support | SA Health. Find out more about working in the Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network, and see what it looks like to work and live in regional Australia at: https:--movetomore.com.au-

Our client, Red Steel Works Pty Ltd. is a prominent Perth based company that specializes in providing reliable and high-quality steel fixing, formwork, precast labor, and scaffolding services for a diverse range of civil, industrial, commercial, and residential projects across Perth and Western Australia.

The client is currently recruiting experienced Formwork Carpenters with a solid background working on residential/ commercial projects to work at the multiple sites.

As a highly motivated and qualified Formwork Carpenter you will require strong technical knowledge of the building and construction industry combined with a high level of attention to detail.  

Minimum Requirements:

AQF Certificate III in relevant trade including 2 years on job training or AQF Certificate IV. At least three years of relevant experience may substitute for the formal qualifications. The position requires at least one year of full -time experience and the ability to work independently to specifications and plans.  

What you will be responsible for:

-	Execute quality formwork carpentry workmanship to the highest level, whilst maintaining our company standards and safety 
-	Read plans and specifications to determine the dimensions, materials required and installation processes to be followed
-	Select appropriate materials for formwork construction, considering factors such as load-bearing capacity, durability, and reusability
-	Create formwork that matches the desired shape and dimensions of concrete structures
-	Interpret plans/engineering and project specifications to meet exacting standards 
-	Construct and repair structural woodwork and equipment from blueprints and oral instructions 
-	Install formwork on-site, pouring concrete into the formwork, and then removing the formwork after the concrete has cured
-	Maintain tools and machinery in safe and efficient operating condition
-	Prepare drawings and sketches of construction and repair projects
-	Estimate costs and orders materials needed.
-	Cut materials, and assemble and nail cut and shaped parts
-	Ensure compliance with relevant building codes, safety standards, and regulations
-	Liaise with clients, other trades in a professional manner
-	Adhere to safety regulations and protocols to maintain a safe working environment
Skills, experience and attributes:
-	Able to read and work from plans
-	Proficiency in carpentry techniques such as cutting, shaping, and joining wood or other materials to construct formwork accurately
-	Ability to manage multiple tasks
-	Must have vast experience in civil formwork, carpentry and be skilled in the use of hand and power tools
-	Ability to troubleshoot and solve problems that may arise during formwork construction
-	Demonstrate an understanding of, and commitment to OH&S principles
-	Able to work unsupervised

The Successful Applicant

You would be required to work in a team environment and would be expected to take on a variety of tasks. You would be required to work at times under pressure and timelines and be available to work in different areas if and when the need arises. The applicant must have an OHS white card and previous experience, preferably in the construction industry.

Please note only short-listed candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.

Stonemason – Eastern Creek NSW

Kogan People Solutions is recruiting for a business specialising in the supply and installation of high-end stone products, including marble, porcelain, and other premium materials. The company provides expert fabrication and installation services, blending craftsmanship with the timeless design of products such as benchtops, stairs, and other elegant interiors for residential and commercial clients.

With a strong focus on quality, detail, and aesthetic excellence, they are currently seeking an experienced and qualified Stonemason to join the team. They are seeking a highly motivated individual who can demonstrate the care and attention to detail that this role requires. The role is full-time and ongoing.

Location – work is based in Eastern Creek NSW, with occasional on-site work.

Salary – negotiable in the range of $80k to $85k plus superannuation per annum.

About the role:

This role is based in a busy factory environment and will involve all aspects of factory work required to complete the job and prepare the goods for installation.

Responsibilities of the job include:

•	Expert cutting, shaping, finishing, polishing and handling natural or engineered stone such as marble, porcelain, granite, quartz and other materials.

•	Utilising a range of equipment and machinery to create stone interiors such as benchtops, stairs, splashbacks, sinks and other products.

•	Study and interpret plans, drawings, and specifications to determine materials required, measurements, and appropriate stonemasonry procedures.

•	Reading and interpreting technical drawings and specifications to ensure precise execution of stone products.

•	Mixing required glue and other adhesives to bond stone surfaces securely and ensure proper assembly during fabrication.

•	Operate hand and power tools in a safe and efficient manner, in compliance with company procedures and WHS regulations such as wearing personal protective equipment (PPE), handling materials properly and other safe work procedures.

•	Maintain cleanliness and order in the work area and assist in site clean-up upon project completion.

To be successfully considered, you:

•	Possess relevant trade Certificate III plus 2 years working experience  or Cert IV, ideally in the field of Stonemasonry (or a closely related building trade) or agreed substitute.

•	Have a minimum of 1 or more years working experience in the field, preferably within a factory setting.

•	Have competence and experience in handling masonry tools and materials.

•	Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to work from technical drawings.

•	Excellent communication skills to communicate effectively.

•	Possess White Card or willing to obtain before starting work.

•	Excellent team skills, patience, and empathy.

•	Have physical strength and stamina to work with and handle heavy materials.

•	Are prompt and reliable, with excellent time management skills.

•	Are eager to secure a full-time salaried position (so this role is not suitable for sub-contractors)

•	Possess a current driver’s license.

•	Forklift license is preferred but not essential.

You must have unrestricted full time Australian working rights to be considered.

Applications

Please respond to the recruiters using the facilities on this site, and ensure you attach your updated CV. 

Kogan People Solutions are grateful for all applications, but kindly note that they will only respond to shortlisted applicants.

Our Company

TerraCom Limited (ASX: TER) is an Australian based mining resources company with a global footprint, comprising a large portfolio of operating assets in Australia and South Africa within the coal sectors. We are a renowned low-cost producer focused on delivering exceptional outcomes from our high yielding diversified asset portfolio for its investors. TerraCom owns and operates the Blair Athol Coal Mine, in Central Queensland. This open-cut thermal coal operation consists of a full suite of mining activities inclusive of dragline, truck and excavator, dozer push, mine site rehabilitation, coal processing, coal crushing, product haulage and train load-out activities.

The Blair Athol Coal mine is located 24km northwest of the family-friendly township of Clermont in Central Queensland, 120 km northwest of Emerald and 275km southwest of Mackay.

TerraCom supports our people to grow, learn and develop their skills to reach their potential. We offer an exciting working environment, with career progression opportunities, as we truly believe that the capability and performance of our people is key to our success. Blair Athol Mine believes in fostering and nurturing each of our team members by providing them with a safe and enjoyable place to work, along with guidance and support from a leader they can rely upon. Come and play a key role in shaping our future!

The Role

We are currently seeking a highly motivated Surveyor Assistant / Technician to join our team at Blair Athol. You will assist the Surveyor in providing support for survey control to facilitate execution of mine activities including topsoil, stripping, overburden removal, coal mining, drilling/blasting, rehabilitation and associated projects around the mine. The right candidate will also forge a pathway towards further qualifications within the mine engineering team.

Responsibilities of the Role will include:

* Provide survey services and set out control points to ensure the accurate location and layout of work within the limits, offsets, grades, profiles and elevations for all mining related processes in accordance with the mine design criteria
* Conduct survey operations with drones, laser scanners and GPS and process the data to meet the required schedules
* Process survey data accurately and complete volume quantities
* Measure distances, angles and variations across site as directed
* Identify & escalate any non-conformance or processes that require corrective action.

Skills and Experience:

* A good work ethic, great communication skills and a desire to learn and grow
* A strong commitment to safety

* Ability to prioritise and schedule work
* Ability to accurately measure and interpret data

Benefits

BUSINESS:  PAPADOPOULOS BROTHERS PTY LTD
ABN: 68 607 569 380
TRADING AS: Meli Annandale
LOCATION: 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038
SALARY: $79,500 – $83,000 + Superannuation (commensurate with experience)
EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Full-time (minimum 38 hours per week)

Job Published: 3 July 2026


ABOUT THE BUSINESS
Meli Annandale is a contemporary neighbourhood café located in Annandale, NSW, providing high-quality breakfast, brunch, and lunch dining within a modern hospitality environment. The café offers a diverse menu featuring freshly prepared contemporary Australian café cuisine, specialty coffee, and seasonal menu offerings, with a strong focus on quality ingredients, presentation, and customer experience.
The business operates a full-service dine-in model with prepared-to-order meals delivered across continuous daily service. Kitchen operations involve fresh ingredient preparation, coordinated food production, and efficient workflow management to meet varying customer demand, particularly during peak breakfast, brunch, and weekend trading periods.
The commercial kitchen operates under established systems and procedures, incorporating food preparation, cooking, plating, stock management, and strict compliance with Australian food safety, hygiene, and workplace health and safety standards to ensure consistent service quality and operational efficiency.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The position of Cook is a hands-on operational role responsible for preparing, cooking, and presenting menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and service requirements within a contemporary café environment. The role requires the ability to manage allocated kitchen sections, maintain consistency across breakfast, brunch, and lunch service, and contribute to the efficient day-to-day operation of a commercial kitchen.
The successful candidate will work collaboratively within a team-based environment, demonstrating initiative in food preparation, coordinating workflow during service, maintaining food quality and presentation standards, and ensuring compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.
The primary place of employment will be Meli Annandale, 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038. From time to time, the successful candidate may also be required to perform duties at the employer's associated hospitality venue, Sabine Bondi, Shop 505/500 Oxford Street, Bondi Junction NSW 2022, to support operational requirements. Duties performed at either location will remain consistent with the position of Cook and will be undertaken under the direction of the employer.
The role also provides ongoing opportunities for professional development through structured on-the-job training and exposure to a range of contemporary café kitchen operations and cooking techniques.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

FOOD PREPARATION AND COOKING
•	Prepare, cook, and present a range of breakfast, brunch, and lunch menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and presentation requirements.
•	Undertake ingredient preparation, including washing, cutting, portioning, marinating, and pre-service mise en place to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Apply appropriate cooking techniques including grilling, frying, roasting, baking, poaching, and sautéing while maintaining consistency in quality and presentation.
•	Follow standardised recipes and portion controls to ensure consistency, minimise wastage, and meet service expectations.
•	Adjust food preparation and cooking methods where required to accommodate service volumes, dietary requirements, and special customer requests.

SERVICE AND KITCHEN OPERATIONS
•	Support efficient kitchen workflow during breakfast, brunch, and lunch service to ensure timely preparation and delivery of meals.
•	Manage allocated kitchen sections, ensuring workstations are organised and service-ready prior to and during operational periods.
•	Communicate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to support efficient service delivery and order accuracy.
•	Assist with menu execution, daily specials, and seasonal menu offerings in accordance with business requirements.
•	Adapt workflow during busy service periods while maintaining food quality, presentation, and operational efficiency.

STOCK CONTROL AND KITCHEN ORGANISATION
•	Assist in receiving, inspecting, and storing deliveries to ensure product quality and compliance with storage requirements.
•	Implement stock rotation practices, including FIFO, to maintain freshness and minimise wastage.
•	Monitor ingredient usage and report stock shortages or inconsistencies to senior kitchen staff.
•	Assist with stocktakes and maintain organised storage areas to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Ensure appropriate labelling, storage, and handling of food products in accordance with food safety standards.

FOOD SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE
•	Maintain compliance with food safety legislation and safe food handling procedures.
•	Maintain high standards of hygiene and cleanliness across workstations, equipment, utensils, and food preparation areas.
•	Monitor storage, cooking, and holding temperatures to ensure compliance with food safety requirements.
•	Follow workplace food safety procedures, including HACCP-based practices where applicable.
•	Comply with Workplace Health and Safety requirements, including the safe operation of commercial kitchen equipment.

GENERAL DUTIES AND TEAM CONTRIBUTION
•	Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient workstation throughout each shift.
•	Follow instructions from senior kitchen staff and management with accuracy and attention to detail.
•	Work collaboratively within a team environment to support efficient kitchen operations during busy service periods.
•	Demonstrate reliability, professionalism, punctuality, and a positive approach to work.
•	Participate in ongoing training and professional development to enhance culinary skills and operational performance.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
•	Relevant qualification in Commercial Cookery (Certificate III or higher) or a closely related field, or a minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience within a commercial kitchen environment.
•	Demonstrated experience preparing and cooking food within a commercial café, restaurant, or hospitality environment.
•	Sound knowledge of food safety standards, kitchen hygiene, and safe food handling practices.
•	Ability to work efficiently within a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment.
•	Availability to work weekends, public holidays, and varied rostered shifts as required.

KEY COMPETENCIES
•	Technical Cooking Proficiency
•	Contemporary Café Food Preparation
•	Recipe Interpretation & Food Presentation
•	Time Management
•	Kitchen Workflow & Operational Awareness
•	Attention to Detail
•	Communication & Team Collaboration
•	Problem Solving
•	Food Safety & Compliance
•	Commitment to Continuous Improvement

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit a one-page CV outlining your relevant experience, qualifications, and availability. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted
